title: LRHE execution evidence record
description: One record per claim verification command that actually ran. The closed, runner-attested shape prevents a model's textual opinion from entering the execution-precedence branch that can force a REFUTED verdict.

run_id.description: Joins the command result to exactly one reviewer run; without it execution could override the wrong claim.

claim_rid.description: Joins the command result to exactly one claim within the run; execution precedence must never apply by inference.

ran.description: Attests that a runner actually invoked the command; only true execution may enter the REFUTED precedence branch.

command.description: Records the non-empty command that ran so the result is reproducible rather than a model's proposed verification.

exit_code.description: Captures the process result independently of prose so success or failure cannot be invented by interpretation.

reproduced.description: States whether the predicted failure occurred; false is load-bearing because it forces the REFUTED verdict.

stdout_sha256.description: Commits to exact standard output without embedding it, making the runner's observed evidence tamper-evident.

stderr_sha256.description: Commits to exact standard error so a claimed process outcome can be checked against its diagnostic evidence.

repo_digest_before.description: Identifies the repository state the command started from so execution evidence cannot silently target another epoch.

repo_digest_after.description: Identifies the repository state after execution so mutations that could change the result remain observable.

runner_version.description: Identifies the implementation that captured the evidence so changes in execution semantics are auditable.

started_at.description: Anchors the execution start in time so stale or reordered evidence can be detected.

finished_at.description: Anchors completion in time so the record proves a bounded runner invocation rather than an unstarted proposal.

case_id.description: Links private audit cases by opaque identifier without exposing corpus identity or allowing a case to substitute for a claim join.

wall_time_s.description: Records observed duration so timeouts and implausibly instant results remain diagnosable.

network.description: Discloses whether external state could have influenced the command result and its reproducibility.

notes.description: Carries runner diagnostics only; it cannot replace any required machine-verifiable execution field.
